comment: Sustainability by design names legislation as one of five reinforcing dimensions and states it deserves equal weight, because the right to operate shared infrastructure, to share data across programmes and to require conformance all rest on it. The architecture chapters then offer no guidance on the legal instruments that deliver it. This is the largest gap between what the draft asserts and what it provides.

public.text: Sustainability by design names legislation as one of five reinforcing dimensions and states it deserves equal weight, because the right to operate shared infrastructure, to share data across programmes and to require conformance all rest on it. The architecture chapters then offer no guidance on the legal instruments that deliver it. This is the largest gap between what the draft asserts and what it provides.
public.suggestedRevision: Add a subchapter on legal instruments for DPI-H, parallel to the governance subchapter, covering at minimum: a duty to connect; a corresponding right to connect on non-discriminatory terms; a statutory basis for processing that does not depend on case-by-case consent; a graduated and proportionate enforcement ladder; a tariff or cost-recovery basis; designated holdership per shared function; accessible dispute resolution; and a revision clause. The Dutch case shows the cost of omission: a national exchange infrastructure was technically completed while its enabling Bill was rejected by the Senate in 2011, after which it has operated on a private-law basis with voluntary participation for fifteen years.
